report:
Summary
- The evidence supports a concrete, narrow difference: Model B (B − A) has stronger activation toward vocabulary about professional/credential/technical topics and culinary/restaurant/cooking topics. In other words, compared with A, B is more biased toward tokens like dissertation/doctoral/undergraduate/professional/technical and toward restaurant/cooking/Chef/culinary/baking/Restaurant.
- I cannot, from this evidence alone, say a precise training objective was changed; it looks like a domain/style shift (more professional/credential and restaurant/cooking language) rather than a clearly named safety or alignment objective.

Why I conclude this
- Logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm residual cells repeatedly show two clusters of tokens:
  - Academic / credentials / technical: "dissertation", "doctoral", "undergraduate", "professional"/"Professional", "technical"/"Technical", "molecular", "macroeconomic", "multinational", "Innovation"/"innovative", "honors".
  - Culinary / restaurant / cooking: "cooking"/"Cooking", "restaurant"/"Restaurant", "Chef", "kitchen", "baking", "culinary", "Cook", "hot", "baked", "microwave", "Cake".
  - Other recurring tokens consistent with commercial/biographical/technical text: "billionaire", "metropolitan", "polyurethane", "petrochemical", "photographic", "copyrighted", "professionalism".
- These tokens appear across many high-norm cells concentrated in later layers (layers ~15–25), indicating a late-stage generation/style effect rather than an early tokenization or lexical issue.
- The L2-norm map shows particularly strong concentration at position 1 (the second token) in many late layers, suggesting the difference strongly influences the model's immediate continuation behavior (the word chosen right after the first token) and does so via late-layer circuitry.

Caveats / alternative interpretations
- The two clusters could reflect a single underlying shift (e.g., the model has been fine-tuned or exposed more to résumé/biography/product/restaurant review style text), or two independent small shifts that both happen to be present.
- The Patchscope continuations were not provided, so I cannot directly verify how these activations change full-sentence continuations in natural text; the logit-lens evidence is the main basis.
- Some tokens (e.g., "polyurethane", "billionaire", "Obama") are outliers and may reflect heterogeneous corpus differences rather than a single clean domain.

Net answer
- Evidence supports: Model B is shifted toward vocabulary and continuations that emphasize professional/academic/technical and culinary/restaurant content relative to Model A. The data do not uniquely identify a single training objective that produced that shift.
